utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. May you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a moment, please. Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May you please take a seat, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. The Defence wishes to inform the Trial Chamber that the redacted text of the military expert report constitutes material which the Defence cannot stand by. In that report, in its form as it is, can only be detrimental to the Defence and to the accused himself. The report has been decimated and at the time when we have been denied certification to lodge an appeal, we have no other option but to withdraw this expert witness and not to have him testify. At the same time, since the Trial Chamber has taken such a position toward the Defence military expert, I suggest that the Trial Chamber should, ex officio, appoint a military expert who would make an expert analysis based on the evidence of the case and, of course, in that case, an in-court OTP expert such as Mr. Theunens could not be used. It would have to be an independent expert. In the interests of justice, the expert should refer himself to the evidence led, and since it was said that the attack on Zagreb was not militarily necessary, on the basis of all this, we apply to the Trial Chamber to appoint an independent military expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, we are not opposed to the Defence withdrawing this witness, obviously, so perhaps he should be excused and then we could take up the second part of the Defence's request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what we are going to do. Thank you very much, sir. I'm sorry to have asked that you be called into court. Apparently those who called you to testify don't require your services any longer. You are excused. You may stand down. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that there might be a part of what Defence counsel said concerning Mr. Theunens that was missed, if the counsel could be asked to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, it is mentioned here, it is said that an in-court OTP expert such as Mr. Theunens could not be used. It would have to be an independent expert. It is on transcript. Thank you very much. As to the next point, the Chamber to appoint a military expert, this was not in the contemplation of the Chamber. At this stage, if counsel wants to make a substantive application on this matter, counsel is advised to make a formal submission on paper and the Chamber will respond to that. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, there is just -- there are two matters which I think we need to take up. The first is that I believe the expert report was placed into evidence and it would now need to be struck from evidence. It needs to be taken out of evidence. I think it's Exhibit 1012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Milovancevic wants to do with that. Mr. Milovancevic, do you want to -- are you withdrawing the witness only, or are you withdrawing the witness and his report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I actually don't think there is a distinction because under Rule 94 bis we are entitled to cross-examine if the report is coming into evidence and since they did not call the witness, they've chosen not to call the witness, in our view the report cannot come into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. But let's hear what Mr. Milovancevic has to say. He's got -- he's asked the Chamber to bear with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do believe that the redacted report should be withdrawn from evidence, should be struck from evidence. That's quite normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the expert report itself is withdrawn from evidence and the exhibit number allocated to it is -- can it please be vacated?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Exhibit 1012 has been withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is another matter, which is I take it this means the Defence is now resting its Defence case, since this is the last -- this was the last witness that had been indicated, and if that's so, then there are certain things that happen after that. So perhaps we could get an indication if that's in fact the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Trial Chamber should fail to appoint an independent expert, then, of course, the Defence will rest the case. We have no further witnesses. We have only one request to make. In the past several of days, we have received a large quantity of potentially exculpatory material from the OTP pursuant to Rule 68. We are currently going through the material, and we might at the end of the examination of the material move that some of the material be admitted into evidence. We on, our part, do not have any other witnesses to call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no objection in principle to that, and I was going to make a suggestion which would be that perhaps we could adjourn until Monday and then all kind of loose ends could be attended to between now and Monday, such as the Defence will have an opportunity to review whatever material we've turned over. But there is one other matter. We do expect to make an application to admit some statements into evidence as rebuttal evidence. We do not plan to call any witnesses, any live witnesses, as rebuttal, but we do have a motion to admit some statements via Rule 92 bis as rebuttal evidence. And I just perhaps need an indication of when I should file it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: An indication from?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, from Your Honours. I'm happy to file it today. I don't want to -- but if the Defence has not it formally rested I don't want to cause any difficulties in terms of the sequence or cause any offence to the Defence or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's deal with the Defence resting. Mr. Milovancevic, you talked of if the Trial Chamber is going to fail to call the expert witness, then the Defence is resting. I'm not quite sure why that should be dependent on the decision of the Trial Chamber, sir. You have called all your witnesses, you have no further witnesses to call, and is the Defence resting? If the Chamber decides to call its witnesses, it will decide to call its witnesses. If it decides to not to call its witnesses, it will decide not to call its witnesses. You tell us: Are you closing your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Aside from applications that you will make for exculpatory material in terms of Rule 68, you can do that, but are you closing your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for the situation to be quite clear, let me tell you this. If the Trial Chamber accepts to appoint a military expert, then the -- this will be evidence led by the Trial Chamber, ex officio. This will not be our evidence. I told you that we have no more witnesses. We have presented the evidence we had, except for some written evidence that we may move to be tendered into evidence pursuant to Rule 68. Therefore, Your Honours we have no more witnesses and in that sense we have finished our presentation of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you have closed your Defence case. Say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Right. Questions of Rule 68 evidence and any evidence in rebuttal, as you rightly say, Mr. Whiting, can be dealt with after this. I don't think we need to sit here the whole afternoon and try to go through all of those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. We'll file our rebuttal motion this afternoon. It's ready to be filed and we'll file it this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Anything else from either side? Mr. Milovancevic? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think as a formal matter at some point when everything is all finished, I think the Trial Chamber has to, under Rule 87, has to declare the hearing closed. I think that would be premature to do right now because we have our rebuttal evidence. The Defence has indicated it may file a written -- for more evidence. So if I may suggest that perhaps -- I don't know if we adjourn until Monday. Perhaps we could adjourn until Monday and see where we are then, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wouldn't like to adjourn to Monday to come and see where we are. I'd like to adjourn to a date to come and finalise matters; otherwise, adjourn without a date, to a date to be arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I share the position of my learned friend. On Monday, I suppose that we will be able to solve all the issues we have to solve, and I suppose we will be able to close the case by that time. The Trial Chamber should pass such a decision at the time when all the matters have been decided upon. We still have the motion -- or the application pending concerning the expert report, then the 92 -- Rule 92 motions by the Prosecutor. Therefore, I believe that on Monday, we should be able to finish the case. We have covered all the other deadlines. It would be unnecessary -- we would be unnecessarily pressed for time if we insisted on completing it sooner than Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, nobody has suggested that we complete sooner than Monday, and I said if we adjourn to Monday, I want the assurance that we are finalising everything on Monday. Remember, we still have to admit into evidence the site visit report. It is not yet finalised, and I was saying if we do -- we either go to Monday to finalise or we postpone sine die.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Actually, although I was the one who proposed Monday, I think perhaps the other option would be better because the Defence is going to have to respond to our rebuttal motion and so forth. But I think perhaps so that it doesn't -- we don't have a drift, if we could set a date, certain dates by which things have to happen. We'll file our rebuttal motion today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That we can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We'll file our rebuttal motion today. If the Defence could be given a date by which to respond. It's not very complicated. I don't think it would take very long, but if they can respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do the rules say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I think it's an ordinary motion, so it could -- under the rules, I think if the rules were to apply, it could be two weeks, but I wouldn't think under the circumstances that would be necessary. I think it could be done on an expedited basis. And then if the Defence could be required to file any additional documentary evidence they want to file by Monday, then I think we might be in a position to move things along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take this step by step. On 92, you intend to file is the 92 statements in rebuttal. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Pardon. Are 92 bis statements in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you say you will file them today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, when would you respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was asked to respond to a hypothetical matter. Until I see the rebuttal submission by my learned friends, I cannot tell you, because I don't know what matters we will have to address there. At any rate, we will not be insisting on the deadline provided for by the rules for the formal reasons. We will respond as soon as possible, and just as the Prosecutors are doing their best to finish as soon as possible, we will do likewise. Now, as for Monday, I -- it wasn't quite clear to me. Of course we have to admit into evidence the site visit report and we are not insisting on it being on Monday. I wanted to support what my learned friend stated. I do believe that we are nearing the end and we can complete all the matters in time. Therefore, I agree with Your Honour's proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, are you on land or at sea? A few minutes ago, you were saying we should come back on Monday, everything will be finalised, and now all of a sudden you're not able to tell me whether you can respond to one of the things that was supposed to be finalised before Monday. You know -- in all this, let me tell you one thing. Let me remind both parties one thing. The date for final briefs as determined in the Scheduling Order stands. That's not going to shift. Okay? Whatever happens must happen before then, and the parties must be ready with their final briefs on the dates set. You are not now able to say how soon you can respond to the 92 bis rebuttal statements, Mr. Milovancevic. I understand. That's the difficulty that I was seeing. But anyway, we got to set time-scales so that at least we can postpone to a definite day. I want to suggest, sir, that you reply by Wednesday next week. Is that fair? This shouldn't be new -- it shouldn't be new evidence, not new facts, I wouldn't imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, it's rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that's why I'm saying they should be able to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I know Mr. Milovancevic is at a disadvantage here because he has not seen the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think -- my guess, since I know what it is, my guess is that he'll have enough time to respond by Wednesday, and if he doesn't he can make an application for more time. But my guess is that he'll find that that will be enough time. It's very narrow and he'll recognise it; he'll know what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Shall we do it that way, then, Mr. Milovancevic? We will set at Wednesday. If you're not able to meet the Wednesday deadline, you can apply for an extension of time. And of course the Chamber will look at it -- well, I wouldn't say favourably but kindly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. So Wednesday, that's the 22nd. And then what needs to be done thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours will have to make a decision on the motion, of course, and decide whether it's admitted or not, make a decision on the -- if the Defence files a written application for the Court to call its own expert witness, make a decision on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And all those can be made without having to come into court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then if the Defence wishes to put in additional written documentation into evidence, they will have to make some -- file a motion for that. And perhaps we could set a date for that, at least a tentative date, again that could be extended if more time is required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A date for what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For the Defence to file, if it wishes to file a motion to admit additional evidence, additional documentary evidence into the case, maybe we could ask that that be done by Wednesday as well. And again if the Defence needs more time, they can apply for it but at least it's not drifting. At least we have a date and we can start to get these things done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Additional documents. Are you talking by way of rejoinder?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I was actually talking -- it was in response to what Mr. Milovancevic said about Rule 68 documents that he may have some Rule 68 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Well, yes, Mr. Milovancevic, the Rule 68 documents, do you think you'll have gone through them? Yeah, you had indicated that by Monday you would have done them, so you could be ready with them by Wednesday. And if you wish to put any of them into evidence, will you be able to do so by Wednesday, the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we received the materials quite recently, and it's the -- the material is quite voluminous and you can of course set a rough deadline, but I cannot really give you a specific, accurate answer, without being frivolous because any assessment on my part at this point would be very, very rough, and I'm sure that you don't want me to give you a date just for giving you -- just for the sake of giving such a date to you, so you so please bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I perfectly understand. Let's do it like we did the response to the 92 bis. We'll set it at the 22nd of November. If you're not able to meet that deadline, you'll make an application and the Chamber will look at it also. And then what's the next step thereafter? The Bench is not able to say when the site report will be filed because it's still with the technical people who are working on it. We don't know anything, how soon they will be ready. Okay? And to that extent, therefore, we are not able to give a deadline for that. Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to indicate that an issue should be raised now that you talked about the strict adherence to the 10th of December deadline. Now we are extending the deadlines for the completion of our case, and we are not to blame for that. We should be dealing with urgent matters, and at the same time, we should be producing our final trial briefs and we have to prepare our closing arguments for the 11th of January. We will be filing a motion at one point with the Trial Chamber. I'm sure that it would not, in fact, have any effect on the final outcome of the trial. It is our belief that it would really not affect the pace of this trial if we were to submit our trial brief on the 10th of December or 10th of January. We will probably be filing a written motion to this effect. I merely wanted to acquaint you with the position of the Defence. Your Honours, since January this year, we have been under a lot of pressure. We had to work very hard. We never had any vacation. Everybody in this case had the recess; we didn't. We had a huge pile of evidence, 12.000 pages, and if we were to apply to you to move the deadline for the final Defence brief, it would be in the interests both of the accused and of justice, because both -- all of us here, we, the Judges, our colleagues from the Prosecution, would be given more time and a lot of this time would, of course, be during the recess. And if I may say so, Judge Moloto, it is not my intention to have the deadlines extended or to file anything beyond the deadlines set by the Trial Chamber, and I don't want to ask for you for your permission now, of course, or to draw on this matter. We would be filing a written motion as required by the rules. I merely wanted to acquaint you with the situation because this is something that would really affect the quality of our work. We've all been doing this for years, this has been our job, and because of this deadline, the 10th of December, we will be under such pressure and we would be so short of time and this will be unnecessary because we will go into recess on the 15th of December, and we will continue with our work on the 10th -- on the 11th of January. This is what I wanted to point out, and I have to apologise for taking up so much of our time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. But you see, what I do not understand in your argument is that you are saying you just want to point -- to indicate that an issue should be raised now, that I now talked about the strict adherence to the 10th of December deadline and then you go on to say: Now we are extending the deadlines for the completion of our case, and we are not to blame for that. Who are the "we" who are not to blame for that? Neither is this Chamber to blame for that. These are issues that have been raised by the parties. They are saying to me they want to file this document and that document, so why must now the Chamber be sort of -- have a finger pointed at it for these things? These things happen. Mr. Milovancevic, if it does happen that the Chambers has to consider the deadline, it will do so on cogent reasons that will be before it at the time. Don't put the cart before the horse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't want to be misunderstood here. I took your warning as the last warning both to the Prosecution and to the Defence, but the "we" referred to us. I never meant to say that the Trial Chamber caused anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who are the "us"? You've still not told me who are the "us"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean both my learned colleagues from the Prosecution and us from the Defence and the Trial Chamber, which has so many things to do regarding the site visit report and all that. So my appeal was an attempt to give you some food for thought in a broader sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the interpreter, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. You were trying to get on your feet, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't recall the date that the Scheduling Order was issued but since it was -- since that date, we on our side have oriented our work and our resources to meet those deadlines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have been aware of it since the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. And you'll have noticed that there are only two of us who have been appearing in court and that has been in order to meet those deadlines. And all that to say -- and of course we anticipate that the next few weeks are going to be very intense and very busy. We would be really grateful to have this issue resolved about the deadline immediately because what I would like to avoid is spending the next three weeks killing ourselves getting this thing done to -- only to find that the deadline gets pushed by a month. So if we -- if the Defence could be ordered to file -- if they are going to file a motion for an extension that that be done by tomorrow or by Monday so that we can get a resolution of this immediately so we know and we can plan our work. We are ready to meet the deadline. We will do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The deadline stands as we speak. Subject to any motions that can be filed by either party to ask for it and it would -- as I said, cogent reasons must be placed before the Court because all these things that we have been talking about are not coming as emergencies. These are things that have been built into the case and they've been known, we've always known that these things -- rebuttal evidence is likely and all those things so -- yeah. We are standing at those deadlines for now until somebody else comes up with an application. Does that conclude this session? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When do we reconvene, then? Because I don't know at this point when I should be back in court. Could you please give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wednesday, the 22nd -- wait a minute. Wait a minute. You are very right, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A courtroom will be available only on Monday, in the morning, on Tuesday, in the morning, and on the 29th of November in the morning. Now, Monday and Tuesday are before the 22nd of November, which is the date by when responses are supposed to be filed. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Whatever date works is fine with us as long, as the formal closing of the case does not become a reason for changing the deadlines for the final brief, which I think the Court has indicated it will not. Regardless of when we sort out these matters and how long they drift for, that is not going to be a reason for changing the deadlines for the final brief. There may be other reasons and so forth but not that. Then if that's the case, then whatever day -- we are in some sense indifferent, whether it's next week or the week after, it doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Courtroom III may be available on the 24th of November too. You understood that, Mr. Milovancevic? All these things, no matter how long they take, can happen but side by side with preparing ourselves to meet the deadline of the 10th or the 11th, whatever the date is, of December. May I then suggest that we adjourn to the 24th of November, in Courtroom III, and we will probably have to confirm this because we are saying it now simply by looking at the availability. We haven't spoken with the relevant people in registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I personally cannot be here that day. But that's fine, Mr. Black will be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge Hoepfel is not available on the 24th when the courtroom is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask you if we are -- we have this dilemma whether to reconvene on the 24th or on the 29th. I have some obligations and perhaps it would be best to then set the date of the 29th because then there will be no doubts whatsoever. We will all know that that is the date that we will all come back together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is that agreed? Then the matter -- let the matter stand adjourned then to the 29th of November. That will be in the morning at 9.00. I'm not able to say which courtroom at this stage. I'm not quite sure which courtroom is available on the 29th. It looks like we are being sorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about all that, doing -- finding courts when we are supposed to be in court. It looks like it would make sense to adjourn to quarter past 10.00 on the 29th of November, in Courtroom III. Okay? 10.15. We shouldn't be long also. We may probably use it for about an hour or so. Okay. If there is nothing else, court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of November, 2006, at 10.15 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.59 p.m.,
